records.description: A weakness has been identified in Linux Foundation Magma up to 1.9.0. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file orc8r/cloud/go/services/obsidian/access/operator.go of the component Obsidian REST. Executing a manipulation of the argument X-Magma-Client-Cert-Serial can lead to authentication bypass by spoofing. The attack can be launched remotely. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A security flaw has been discovered in Linux Foundation Magma up to 1.9.0. The affected element is an unknown function of the file orc8r/lib/go/registry/interceptors.go. Performing a manipulation results in hard-coded credentials. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was identified in Linux Foundation Magma up to 1.9.0. Impacted is the function handleReact of the file nms/server/main/routes.ts of the component NMS. Such manipulation leads to cross site scripting. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was determined in Linux Foundation Magma up to 1.9.0. This issue affects the function hostOrgMiddleware of the file nms/server/host/middleware.ts of the component Host Middleware. This manipulation of the argument role causes missing authorization. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Zr.Admin.NET commit 1845017 through commit eb9228a contains a missing authorization vulnerability in TasksController.Get that allows any logged-in user to read scheduled task details without the monitor:job permission. Attackers can obtain task ids from the unprotected /monitor/jobLog/list endpoint and retrieve job parameters, API URLs, cron expressions, and stored SQL statements.

Zr.Admin.NET commit af07ffc through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in SysProfileController.UpdateProfile that allows any authenticated user to modify other accounts via UserId. Attackers can set the administrator's phone number to one they control, request an SMS code via /checkMobile, and log in through /PhoneLogin to take over the administrator account.

Zr.Admin.NET commit 0ee1ab8 through commit eb9228a contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows any logged-in user to read arbitrary server files via the path parameter of /common/DownloadFile. Attackers can supply absolute paths or ../ sequences to read appsettings files and use the JwtSettings SecretKey to forge administrator tokens.

Zr.Admin.NET commit e6ceaf4 through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in FrontArticleController that allows authenticated users to change other users' article visibility and pin state. Attackers can send PUT /front/article/changePublic with their own UserId in the body to make private articles public, then read them anonymously via GET /front/article/{id}.

Zr.Admin.NET commit 85cff6a through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /workflow/instance/{instanceId} that lets logged-in users view others' workflow instances. Authenticated low-privilege attackers can enumerate sequential instance IDs to read other users' approval requests, including submitted form contents, applicant details and approval records.

A vulnerability was found in vllm-project vllm 0.30.0/0.31.0. This vulnerability affects unknown code of the file single_type_kv_cache_manager.py of the component Common Prefix Handler. The manipulation results in race condition. The attack may be performed from remote. Attacks of this nature are highly complex. It is stated that the exploitability is difficult. The exploit has been made public and could be used. Upgrading to version 0.32.0 is able to resolve this issue. The patch is identified as e687a251bb056fa527846633f7a1b0a6c0f42374. You should upgrade the affected component.

A vulnerability has been found in sigoden dufs up to 0.46.0. This affects an unknown part of the file src/server.rs of the component WebDAV COPY Operation Handler. The manipulation leads to incorrect authorization. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. Upgrading to version 0.47.0 is able to mitigate this issue. The identifier of the patch is fba13dffb9c65b5e5e26419f64de709200277a04. It is advisable to upgrade the affected component.

A flaw has been found in D-Link DIR-600L 2.17b02. Affected by this issue is the function hnap_main of the file htdocs/cgibin of the component HNAP Handler. Executing a manipulation can lead to stack-based buffer overflow. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used.

A vulnerability was detected in D-Link DIR-600L 2.17/2.17b02. Affected by this vulnerability is the function authenticationcgi_main of the file authentication.cgi. Performing a manipulation of the argument id/password results in stack-based buffer overflow. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit is now public and may be used.

A vulnerability was detected in TRENDnet TEW-657BRM 1.00.1. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file /usr/sbin/upgrade_flash.cgi. Performing a manipulation of the argument boundary results in stack-based buffer overflow. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The vendor explains: ""I am not able to confirm if such vulnerability exists as the product has been EOL for more than 15 years. We will send out an announcement letting customers know."

A security vulnerability has been detected in TRENDnet TEW-657BRM 1.00.1. This vulnerability affects the function sprintf of the file /setup.cgi of the component mini_httpd. Such manipulation leads to out-of-bounds write. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The vendor explains: ""I am not able to confirm if such vulnerability exists as the product has been EOL for more than 15 years. We will send out an announcement letting customers know." This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

Dancer versions before 1.3400 for Perl pass unvalidated session ids from the session cookie to the session engine.

read_session_id returns the cookie value as the session id without checking its characters, and Dancer hands it to the session engine to load the session.

A remote attacker may cause path traversal or injection in a session engine that uses the id in a file path, cache command or query without checking it.

Kroki before 0.36.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the /dbml/svg endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject javascript: hyperlinks by supplying crafted DBML table url, headercolor, or TableGroup color settings. Attackers can send a crafted SVG link that, when opened and the table header clicked, executes attacker JavaScript in the Kroki origin.

A vulnerability was found in sergix44 XBackBone up to 3.8.2. Impacted is the function MediaController::getRawById of the file app/Controllers/MediaController.php. The manipulation results in cross site scripting. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

A security vulnerability has been detected in sox_ng up to 14.8.1. Affected by this issue is the function read_samples_voc of the file src/voc.c of the component VOC Decoder. Such manipulation leads to out-of-bounds write. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The name of the patch is 0b40408b. A patch should be applied to remediate this issue. The vendor was contacted early, responded in a very professional manner and quickly released a fixed version of the affected product.

A weakness has been identified in Wuxi Wubang Security Software Wubang Five-in-One Safety Production Management Information System up to 3.5. Affected by this vulnerability is the function DiyFileUpload of the file /ws.asmx. This manipulation causes unrestricted upload. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was found in Kingston FURY CTRL RGB Control Software up to 2.0.66.0. The impacted element is an unknown function in the library NTIOLib_X64.sys of the component IOCTL Handler. Performing a manipulation results in exposed ioctl with insufficient access control. The attack is only possible with local access.

A security vulnerability has been detected in Mereithhh VanBlog up to 0.54.0. This vulnerability affects the function fs.readFileSync of the file local.provider.ts of the component Custom Page Handler. The manipulation of the argument path leads to path traversal. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. Upgrading to version test-20261013 is able to resolve this issue. The identifier of the patch is d63aa163f10b6dc1080e2368fe8e71aa95b765cb. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

The BuddyForms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'buddyforms_form_content' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.10.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable when a form configured with the public_submit option is published — a condition met by the plugin's bundled Post Simple template out of the box.

This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the target CF7 form to have the 'Save every step' option enabled and the Database for Contact Form 7 companion plugin to be active with its 'Expandable' ta

The FV Player 8 plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'fv_player_videos' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.1.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the administrator-controlled "Allow visitors to upload videos to their profile" setting to be enabled, without which the vulnerable save routine is inaccessible to Subsc

A weakness has been identified in Mereithhh VanBlog up to 0.54.0. This affects an unknown part of the file packages/server/src/types/access/access.ts of the component Image Upload Endpoint. Executing a manipulation can lead to cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was identified in Tenda AC18 15.03.05.05_multi/15.03.05.19 Build 6318. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file /cgi-bin/upgrade of the component Firmware Upgrade Handler. Such manipulation of the argument upgradeFile leads to insufficient verification of data authenticity. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

HTTP::Session versions before 0.43 for Perl allow memcached command injection via unfiltered session ids in HTTP::Session::Store::Memcached.

The session id from the client's cookie reaches memcached unchanged as the cache key.

A CR and LF in the session id end the cache command early, and the server reads the bytes after them as further commands.

The Shipo plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in versions 1.6 through 1.8.0. This is due to the `authenticate_rest_user()` function parsing the `LOGGED_IN_COOKIE` value and authenticating the named user without verifying the cookie's cryptographic signature. The function's intended `/wp-json/shipo/` route restriction can also be bypassed by placing that substring in the query string of an unrelated REST endpoint. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers who know an existing username to impersonate that user, including an administrator, and perform authorized

The MemberDash plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.7. This is due to a mass-assignment vulnerability in the `user_account_manager()` function's edit_profile branch, where all submitted `$_POST` fields are iterated and directly assigned to the current member object via the `MS_Model` `__set()` magic method with no field allowlist and no capability or ownership check on the submitted `id` parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject an arbitrary user ID via the `id

Dokploy before 0.31.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in getComposeContainerCommand() that allows authenticated organization members to execute shell commands via the serviceName parameter. Attackers can store serviceName values with shell metacharacters through backup.create or backup.update tRPC procedures, executing commands as root when scheduled backups run and taking over the host via the mounted Docker socket.

Ettercap through 0.8.5.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dissector_mountd() in src/dissectors/ec_mountd.c that validates RPC credential and directory lengths independently rather than against the packet end. Network-adjacent attackers can send a crafted MOUNT MNT call to read up to 100 bytes past the heap buffer, leaking memory to the console and logs.

Ettercap through 0.8.5.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dissector_socks() in src/dissectors/ec_socks.c that allows network-adjacent attackers to read heap memory via unchecked SOCKS5 username/password lengths. Attackers can send a crafted SOCKS5 authentication packet observed by Ettercap to read up to 255 bytes past the heap buffer, disclosing memory printed and logged as captured credentials.

Axeloz Filesharing before 2.14.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by storing raw HTML or javascript: Markdown links in bundle descriptions. Recipients viewing the public bundle preview page execute the script via Alpine x-html, letting attackers steal the owner_token from localStorage and issue owner-scoped requests against victim bundles.

Frappe india-payroll before 16.0.4 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the get_employee_details, compute_tax_comparison and set_tax_regime methods of tax_regime_selector.py that allows authenticated low-privileged users to access other employees' payroll data. Attackers can supply another employee identifier to read base pay and earning and deduction components, or change the tax regime on draft Salary Structure Assignments to affect tax withholding.

Pulse from 5.0.17 before 6.8.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the /api/ai/approvals endpoints that allows authenticated viewer-level users to manage approval requests. Attackers can list pending requests to expose proposed commands and targets, and approve or deny other users' requests, altering decision and audit state.

A vulnerability was identified in CoolerMaster MASTERPLUS+ 1.9.6. This affects the function sub_11504 in the library WinRing0x64.sys of the component Device Driver. The manipulation of the argument PhysicalAddress leads to incorrect default permissions. The attack can only be performed from a local environment. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A flaw has been found in Opixido OCMS up to b7c15660aba83d96677c1a9abaa69c082a24f21c. This impacts an unknown function of the file admin/TUI/index.php of the component Admin TUI. This manipulation of the argument img causes cross site scripting. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Continious delivery with rolling releases is used by this product. Therefore, no version details of affected nor updated releases are available. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

The Cloud Storage Manager for Fluent Forms – Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, S3 Uploads plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write in all versions up to, and including, 1.2.0. This is due to missing authorization checks on the `connection/{driver}/save` and `/download/single-file` REST endpoints, combined with insufficient path validation in the Google Drive `downloadFile()` function, where the Google Drive metadata `name` value is concatenated into a local path without `basename()`, `sanitize_file_name()`, or canonical path validation. This makes it possible for unauthenticat

@kolkov/angular-editor before 3.0.3 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in refreshView() that writes HTML from ngModel or reactive form controls to innerHTML without DomSanitizer, bypassing the default sanitize option. Attackers can store HTML with event-handler attributes in content later loaded into the editor to execute script in the application's origin for users opening it.

@kolkov/angular-editor before 3.0.4 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in toggleEditorMode() that assigns source view text to innerHTML without DomSanitizer sanitization. Attackers can induce users to paste HTML with event handlers such as img onerror into source mode, executing script in the application's origin when toggling views.

in Cervantes version v1.3-beta could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code in another user's browser with elevated privileges

A vulnerability was detected in hrshadhin CloudSchool up to 3.0.1. This affects an unknown function of the file app/Http/Controllers/Backend/EventController.php of the component Event Description Handler. The manipulation of the argument data results in cross site scripting. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A security vulnerability has been detected in Edimax BR6478ACV2 1.23. The impacted element is the function formPPTPSetup of the file webs. The manipulation of the argument pptpUserName leads to buffer overflow. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

JSON::XS versions from 3.0 before 4.05 for Perl read freed stack memory when a FREEZE result's serialisation grows the Perl stack under allow_tags in encode_rv.

With allow_tags, an object's FREEZE method is called in list context and each returned value is encoded through a saved Perl stack pointer. When encoding a returned value calls back into Perl, through TO_JSON under convert_blessed or another FREEZE, and that callback grows the stack, the stack is reallocated while the saved pointer still refers to the freed block.

Encoding such objects reads freed memory, and encode can return undef

JSON::XS versions from 3.04 before 4.05 for Perl write one byte past a heap buffer when appending a one-byte chunk in incr_parse.

The incremental buffer grows to one and a half times the length it must hold, with no room reserved for the terminating NUL. For an empty buffer and a one-byte chunk that request is one byte, which a buffer whose front was removed by earlier decodes can already have, so nothing is reallocated and the NUL lands one byte past the allocation.

JSON::XS versions from 4.0_00 before 4.05 for Perl corrupt the incremental buffer length by chopping past its end in incr_skip after a top-level number.

The incremental parser scans any run of digits, signs, dots and exponent markers as one number, but the decoder stops at the end of a valid number, so the parser keeps an offset into bytes it has not decoded. It then empties the buffer without clearing those bytes, and a later incr_parse call without new input reads them again and moves the offset past the end of the buffer. incr_skip, the documented recovery after an error, removes that many

JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded part of a rejected long string in decode_str.

A string is decoded through a fixed-size buffer (16 KiB in 4.04), and each time the buffer fills its contents move into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the string is then rejected for a control character, an invalid escape, malformed UTF-8 or the end of the input.

A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains the decoded part of each rejected string, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.

JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow stack exhaustion via nested tagged values under allow_tags in decode_tag.

With allow_tags, "(" starts a tagged value. Its tag and value are decoded recursively, and each can start another tagged value. Unlike arrays and objects, this nesting is not counted against max_depth.

A run of "(" bytes exhausts the C stack and triggers an uncatchable segmentation fault regardless of max_depth.

JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl leak the decoded key of an object rejected for a missing colon in decode_hv.

Unless it is short plain ASCII, a quoted key is decoded into a new scalar. Nothing frees that scalar when the object is rejected for a missing ':' after the key.

A process that keeps running after a failed decode retains one key per rejected document, with its size chosen by the sender. Repeated requests exhaust process memory.

JSON::XS versions before 4.05 for Perl allow memory exhaustion by buffering incremental input past max_size after a NUL byte in incr_parse.

The parser appends each chunk to its buffer and compares max_size with how far it has progressed, not with the buffer length. It treats a NUL byte as the end of the input, so a NUL within the first max_size bytes keeps it short of the limit. The buffer keeps growing, and incr_skip cannot remove the NUL.

A peer streaming data to an incr_parse consumer can exhaust process memory regardless of max_size.

A weakness has been identified in Akaunting up to 3.3.0. The affected element is the function calculation_to_quantity of the file helpers.php of the component Invoice Item Validation. Executing a manipulation of the argument quantity can lead to numeric range comparison without minimum check. The attack may be performed from remote. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A security flaw has been discovered in yangzongzhuan RuoYi up to 4.8.3. Impacted is the function VelocityUtils.getFileName of the file VelocityUtils.java of the component Code Generator. Performing a manipulation of the argument className results in path traversal. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely.

The Flatsome theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'data-text-sec', 'data-title', and 'title' Attributes via Custom HTML Block in all versions up to, and including, 3.20.12 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. A vulnerability has been found in projectworlds Visitor Management System 1.0. This issue affects the function mysqli_query of the file /img/user%20page.php of the component Login Endpoint. Such manipulation of the argument Username leads to sql injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

In versions 4.0.4 and below, the JavaScript implementation (browser.js, used by browser bundlers and on Node.js versions without a working native crypto.createECDH) did not validate peer public keys in ECDH.prototype.computeSecret or ECDH.prototype.setPublicKey. The peer point was multiplied by the local private key without checking that it was on the configured curve or in its prime-order subgroup. The Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 was distributed with a hidden update mechanism that fetched Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 updates from its author's own server instead of WordPress.org, which was used to push a backdoored build to sites, allowing the attacker controlling that server to inject arbitrary content into pages and to deliver arbitrary code to affected sites.

The WP Ultimate CSV Importer  WordPress plugin before 9.3 does not escape values from imported files before using them in SQL queries when importing LifterLMS content, allowing high privilege users such as admin, including the administrator of a single site on a multisite network, to perform SQL injection attacks.

The WP Ultimate CSV Importer  WordPress plugin before 9.2, WP Ultimate CSV Importer Pro WordPress plugin before 9.0.7 do not protect the files created by their single post export feature, writing them to a publicly accessible location under a predictable name, allowing unauthenticated attackers to download the content and custom fields of any exported post, including non-public content.

The Lightbox with PhotoSwipe WordPress plugin before 5.19.0 does not properly sanitise link titles and other caption sources before inserting them as HTML into the image lightbox caption, allowing unauthenticated users to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks via comments.

The Checkout Files Upload for WooCommerce WordPress plugin before 2.4.1 does not verify that a file uploaded at checkout is really one of its allowed image types, and serves stored uploads inline using their detected content type, allowing unauthenticated users to upload an HTML file disguised as an image that executes JavaScript in the browser of a shop manager or administrator who opens it from the order screen.
This is a regression of CVE-2025-4212, reintroduced in 2.4.0.

The SEOJuice WordPress plugin before 2.12.0 does not correctly restrict a REST API authentication filter, disabling WordPress's REST nonce protection for the whole site and allowing unauthenticated attackers to perform any cookie-authenticated REST action, including creating a new administrator account, by tricking a logged-in administrator into opening a crafted page (CSRF).

The Swipe WordPress plugin through 1.4 does not properly authenticate a login request before issuing a WordPress session cookie, allowing unauthenticated attackers to log in as an existing user, including an administrator, when that user has an active app session.

The Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 does not check whether a user may publish posts when duplicating one, allowing users of a role an administrator has given Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 access to, such as Contributors, to create published posts, including posts attributed to other users.

The Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 does not check that a user duplicating a post is allowed to edit it, which, when the slug takeover option is enabled, allows users of a role an administrator has given Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 access to, such as Contributor, to move any readable post off its permalink and publish their copy at that address.

The Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 does not perform a capability check when saving its global settings, relying only on its own role-access list, which allows users of any role an administrator has given Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 access to, as low as Subscriber, to overwrite those settings, including the role-access list itself.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not enforce the acting user's publish and post-type restrictions on an AJAX save action, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to publish their own content and change its post type (for example to a product) without holding the required capabilities.

The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not perform a capability or nonce check on an AJAX action available to unauthenticated users, and does not restrict the status of the posts it returns by ID, allowing unauthenticated users to disclose the content of unpublished (draft and pending) posts.

The Chargely Free Subscriptions For Woocommernce WordPress plugin through 1.0 does not perform any authorization check on a REST API route that returns its stored configuration, allowing unauthenticated attackers to retrieve the live WooCommerce REST API consumer key and secret it holds, which grant read and write access to the whole store.

The Countdown, Coming Soon, Maintenance  WordPress plugin through 3.0.8 does not check that the user is allowed to browse content before returning post titles from one of its AJAX actions, allowing any authenticated user, such as a subscriber, to list the titles of published entries of any post type, including types that WordPress does not expose to them. Draft, private and pending content is not returned; only published entries are disclosed.

The Countdown, Coming Soon, Maintenance  WordPress plugin through 3.0.8 does not perform authorization or nonce checks when saving countdown data on post save, and its output-sanitization allowlist permits script tags, allowing users with Author-level access and above to store arbitrary web scripts that execute when the affected content is viewed on the front end or in an administrator session.

The Email Marketing 4Dem WordPress plugin through 2.0.5 does not perform authorization or capability checks on several of its AJAX actions, allowing unauthenticated users to destroy its stored configuration and delete its records.

The Email Marketing 4Dem WordPress plugin through 2.0.5 does not perform authorization or capability checks on several of its AJAX actions and REST routes, allowing unauthenticated users to disclose the Email Marketing 4Dem WordPress plugin through 2.0.5's stored configuration and data and to modify its stored settings.

The AutomatorWP Pro plugin for WordPress' webhook addon is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.4. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to reset the password of any WordPress account, including administrators, resulting in full account takeover. This is only exploitable when an administrator has configured an automation pairing a Receive Webhook trigger — with an 'Is the user ID' field — to an Update-User action whose User ID field is left bla

The Optimole – Optimize Images | Convert WebP & AVIF | CDN & Lazy Load | Image Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the replace_urls_in_value function in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.19. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Successful exploitation requires PEAR's Archive_Tar library to be present and loadable on the host (common in official WordP

PrestaShop before 8.2.9 and 9.2.1 contains an authorization flaw in the Webservice API that allows an attacker holding a key restricted to one shop to act on data of every shop by submitting requests with id_shop=all or id_shop_group=N, which expand the shop context without validating the key's actual shop associations and cause shopHasRight() to evaluate the expanded set as a disjunction. Attackers can exploit this flaw via classes/webservice/WebserviceRequest.php to read, modify, or delete data belonging to shops they are not authorized for, including full customer records such as email addr

PrestaShop before 8.2.9 and 9.2.1 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows an authenticated Webservice API key holder to read and modify customer records belonging to any shop in a multi-shop installation. Attackers can exploit the missing record-level shop ownership check in shopHasRight() and saveEntityFromXml() to read sensitive customer data such as password hashes and secure keys, and change a customer's email and password via create, update, and delete requests, resulting in account takeover.

A flaw has been found in projectworlds Visitor Management System 1.0. This vulnerability affects the function mysqli_query of the file actionpage.php. A remote attacker can block a server event loop with a crafted compressed request body or WebSocket message, and a malicious server can similarly block a client. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4.

Authenticated members can share the note and send the public blob link to a victim, whose browser executes the script to mint a non-expiring API token granting read and write access to the victim's notes.

NginxPulse 1.5.0 before 1.6.26 contains an unauthenticated sql injection vulnerability that allows remote attackers to append SQL via the id and locationType parameters of /api/stats/:type. Attackers can close the quoted table-name identifier and use error-based output to read database contents, and read or write server files via PostgreSQL superuser functions.

FileCodeBox 2.2.1 through 2.8.4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in renderMarkdownPreview, which returns unsanitized text when the marked parser throws. Unauthenticated attackers can share text with thousands of nested blockquote markers followed by HTML payloads, executing script that steals the admin token from localStorage.

PMail 2.5.0 through 2.9.8 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject scripts by sending unsanitized HTML through /api/email/send. Attackers can embed event-handler payloads like img onerror that execute when administrators view the message, enabling privileged API calls such as password changes for account takeover.

PMail 2.9.1 through 2.9.8 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because the /attachments/{id}/{cid} endpoint returns email attachments verbatim with the sender-supplied Content-Type after cid: references are rewritten into attachment links. Unauthenticated SMTP senders can email a text/html attachment and a page-covering cid link, so a recipient who clicks the message runs script in their webmail session to change passwords, including the administrator's.

Seafile SeaDoc converter 2.0.4 before 2.0.11 and 3.0.0 before 3.0.8 contains an absolute path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers holding a public share token to execute code. Attackers supply an absolute filename to /api/v1/confluence-to-wiki/ to extract a ZIP from download_url into the Python library path, then trigger the module's import via a file-convert request.

Keep 0.34.10 through 0.55.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in its CEL-to-SQL converter, which inserts bracket-indexed JSON keys from CEL filters unescaped into JSON path expressions for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL. Authenticated users with read:alert permission can submit crafted CEL expressions to /alerts/query or the cel parameter of /incidents, using result counts as a boolean oracle to extract other tenants' alerts and password hashes.

Tactical RMM 0.17.0 through 1.6.1 contains an arbitrary file read in the /reporting/templates/preview/ endpoint because WeasyPrint resolves file:// links in user-supplied template_md and embeds the files in the returned PDF. Users with report management permission can read the Django SECRET_KEY, reused as the NATS password, and publish runscript commands to every managed agent.

Dromara free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to access code-protected shares because share codes are enforced only client-side. Attackers knowing a share ID can call the share items and download endpoints to list and download files without the code, even on preview-only shares.

Dromara free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows registered users to run script by uploading HTML files served inline as text/html. Dromara free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in FileStreamController.preview that allows unauthenticated attackers to download stored files. Authenticated attackers can upload script-bearing SVG images that execute when victims view them, stealing the non-HttpOnly f-session cookie to hijack accounts.

Unauthenticated D-Bus methods pass caller-controlled URL or .rpm path patterns into a root-privileged cmdline package loader that may store fetched content in a world-readable cache without size limits, or open local paths as root, allowing a local attacker to disclose privileged content and to deny service via disk exhaustion.

Indico is a feature-rich event management system. Prior to version 3.3.14, due to a path traversal vulnerability when building an "offline copy" of an event, a malicious event manager has the ability to retrieve the content of any local file that's readable by the user running Indico on the server. This issue has been patched in version 3.3.14.

Attackers can compute the creation minute and forge the md5Id token to access and read a shared calendar's iCal feed without authorization.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated general administrators to inject arbitrary SQL by setting the personsSort session value, which is concatenated unsanitized into ORDER BY clauses in MdlUser.php and MdlSpace.php. Attackers can craft a CSV cell containing an attribute-breakout payload that is rendered verbatim and executed in the browser of the administrator performing the import, leading to arbitrary script execution in the administrative context.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to access another user's private mail by supplying a crafted reloadMailTypeId parameter to Ctrl::getCurObj() without a readRight() ownership check in CtrlMail.php. Attackers can manipulate the mail identifier value, such as reloadMailTypeId=mail-1, to retrieve the title and body of private messages belonging to other users, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive communications.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows remote attackers to redirect users to arbitrary external URLs by manipulating the objUrl parameter in Ctrl.php's redir() function. Attackers can craft login links with objUrl set to a malicious site, causing the application to issue an HTTP 302 redirect to that external URL, which can be abused for phishing and credential theft.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a predictable token generation vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to access private calendar data by exploiting a missing dateCrea value that causes the md5Id token to collapse to md5(calendarId.userId), both small enumerable integers. Attackers can compute valid tokens and request the misc&action=DisplayIcal endpoint with a forged md5Id to read any user's private calendar events without authentication.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to forge privileged actions such as administrator user creation by merging $_GET and $_POST parameters without requiring an anti-CSRF token. Attackers can craft a malicious link or auto-navigating page that issues a plain GET request, exploiting the lack of CSRF protection and SameSite=Lax cookie behavior on top-level navigations to create unauthorized administrator accounts.

picoquic before 2026.11.05.3e2e3d3 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in picoquic_decode_time_stamp_frame() that allows remote QUIC peers to corrupt stored timestamps by sending oversized TIME_STAMP values. Attackers on connections negotiating the TIME_STAMP extension can send large values shifted by ack_delay_exponent to wrap the result, corrupting RTT and bandwidth estimation and degrading congestion control.

MRBS before 1.13.0 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect reset links by forging the Host header when $url_base is unset. Attackers can request a reset for a victim so AuthDb::notifyUser() emails a link pointing to their host, capturing the reset key when opened to take over accounts including administrators.

MRBS before 1.13.0 contains a CSV formula injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject spreadsheet formulas because the escape() function in web/report.php fails to neutralize leading formula characters. Attackers can store formulas in booking names, descriptions or custom fields that execute when privileged users open exported CSV reports, enabling data exfiltration or command execution via DDE.

MRBS before 1.13.0 contains an LDAP injection vulnerability in web/lib/MRBS/Auth/AuthLdap.php that interpolates unescaped login usernames into DN search and group-membership filters. Attackers with valid directory credentials outside the required group can submit crafted usernames that make the group filter always true, bypassing access restrictions.

Gameyfin before 2.6.2 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass login-required mode by calling Hilla endpoints annotated with @AnonymousAllowed. Attackers can POST to synchronous endpoint methods such as GameEndpoint.sync, which LiveSubscriptionSecurity never checks, to retrieve game catalog metadata, libraries, platforms, plugins and game requests.

agent-device from 0.21.36 before 0.21.37 contains a local file disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated remote callers to read daemon-host files by opening file:// URLs. Attackers can send an open command with a file:// target through /rpc, then issue snapshot to read any plaintext file readable by the daemon account.

AiSOC 12.1.0 before 23.3.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to query the enrichment service through Next.js console rewrite routes. Attackers can send requests to /api/v1/enrichment/lookup or /api/v1/enrichment/bulk to retrieve threat-intelligence results and set force to true to consume commercial provider API quota.

Goose CLI 1.35.0 before 1.53.0 contains a local code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run commands by setting diff.external in a repository's .git/config. Attackers can ship a crafted repository that, when the victim runs goose review, executes git diff without --no-ext-diff, running commands as the user and exposing credentials and provider API keys.

SQLBot through 1.10.3 contains a weak password hashing vulnerability that stores local account passwords in sys_user.password as unsalted MD5 digests via md5pwd() in security.py. Attackers who obtain the user table can recover passwords, including administrator passwords, using precomputed tables or GPU cracking, since identical passwords produce identical hashes.

C-Kermit before 11.1.515 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in putsrv() in ckcfns.c that allows malicious peers to write past the srvcmd buffer by sending crafted packets. Attackers can use Kermit repeat-count compression in server command, GET, or file-header packets to write attacker-chosen bytes beyond the heap buffer on servers or receiving instances.

C-Kermit 6.0.192 before 11.1.515 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows Kermit clients to run shell commands on servers with host commands disabled by abusing REMOTE QUERY evaluation. Attackers can send a REMOTE QUERY invoking the command function, or define a macro via REMOTE ASSIGN and call execute to reach RUN, bypassing the nopush restriction and DISABLE HOST.

C-Kermit before 11.1.515 contains an OS command injection vulnerability that allows remote clients to execute shell commands by supplying unquoted arguments to REMOTE WHO or REMOTE SPACE. Attackers can append shell metacharacters to arguments passed through WHOCMD or SPACM2 to syscmd(), executing commands on the server host even when DISABLE HOST is set.

C-Kermit 8.0.200 before 11.1.515 contains a buffer overflow vulnerability in getreply() in ckcftp.c that allows malicious FTP servers to overwrite client memory by sending overlong security replies. Attackers controlling or intercepting an FTP server can send long PBSZ replies after AUTH TLS, or long ADAT replies in GSSAPI, Kerberos 4, and SRP builds, overflowing the static reply_buf with attacker-controlled bytes.

C-Kermit 6.0.192 before 11.1.515 contains a buffer overflow vulnerability in tn_snenv() in ckctel.c that allows malicious Telnet servers to corrupt client memory via crafted NEW-ENVIRON SEND subnegotiation. Malicious or machine-in-the-middle servers can send oversized variable names before authentication, overflowing a 16-byte stack buffer and a miscomputed heap buffer to corrupt stack and heap memory.

C-Kermit 8.0.200 before 11.1.515 contains a path traversal vulnerability in doftpget() in ckcftp.c that allows malicious FTP servers to write files outside the intended directory. Attackers can return absolute paths, tilde names, or dot-dot components in NLST or MLSD listings during MGET /RECURSIVE to overwrite files like .bashrc, leading to code execution.

C-Kermit 11.0.506 before 11.1.515 contains a RECEIVE CONFIRM bypass vulnerability that allows malicious Kermit servers to write unrequested files without prompting by abusing recursive GET root computation in ckcfns.c. Attackers can send files such as .ssh/authorized_keys or shell startup files under the current directory, which rq_under_root() accepts silently, enabling persistent access or code execution.

C-Kermit from 6.0.192 before 11.1.515 contains a file collision protection bypass that allows malicious senders to append data to existing files by marking transfers as RESEND. The gattr() function in ckcfn3.c clears the REJECT discard flag and switches to APPEND without a RECEIVE CONFIRM prompt, letting attackers modify files such as shell startup files.
